title: Instrument families
examples: Teacher, what is the difference between woodwind and brass instruments?
Can you show me an example of a string instrument?
Which family does the trumpet belong to?

explain.say: Today we will learn about instrument families in music.

draw.text: Instrument Families: Strings, Woodwind, Brass, Percussion

explain.say: Strings instruments make sound by vibrating tight wires or strings.
Woodwind instruments make sound by blowing air across a reed or a hole.

draw.text: Woodwind: Blowing air through a tube

explain.say: Brass instruments get their sound from buzzing your lips into a mouthpiece.
Percussion instruments create sound by being hit or shaken.

draw.text: Percussion: Hit or shaken to make sound

explain.say: When you hear a marching band, you hear all four families working together.

faq.q: What is the difference between woodwind and brass instruments?
faq.a: Woodwind instruments use air blown across a reed or hole to make sound. Brass instruments use buzzing your lips into a mouthpiece to make sound.
asks: How do brass instruments make noise?

faq.q: Do all string instruments use bows?
faq.a: No, some string instruments like the guitar are plucked or strummed. Instruments like the violin are often played with a bow.
asks: Can I play a string instrument without a bow?
What do I use to make a guitar sound?

faq.q: Are there any instruments that fit into more than one family?
faq.a: Some instruments can be played in different ways, changing their family classification. However, we usually group them by their main sound source.
asks: Is the harp a string or percussion?
Can an instrument be in two families?

faq.q: What is the main job of a percussion instrument?
faq.a: The main job is to create rhythm by being hit, shaken, or scraped. They are great for keeping time in music.
asks: What do I use to keep the beat?
How do I make a drum sound?

faq.q: Does the size of the instrument tell you what family it is?
faq.a: No, the size does not always tell you the family. For example, a small flute and a large tuba are very different families.
asks: Does size relate to the family?

facts: Strings instruments vibrate wires to create musical tones.
Woodwind instruments require air blown through a specific opening.
Brass instruments use the player's lips to create a buzzing sound.
Percussion instruments create sound through impact or shaking.

quiz.say: A flute belongs to which family?
quiz.why: The flute makes sound by blowing air across a whistle-like opening, which is how woodwinds work.

wrong.1: Strings vibrate wires, but the flute does not have wires.
wrong.2: Brass instruments require buzzing your lips, which the flute does not need.
wrong.3: Percussion instruments must be hit or shaken, which the flute is not.

quiz.say: The trumpet is an example of which instrument family?
quiz.why: The trumpet creates its sound by buzzing the lips into a mouthpiece, which is the key for brass instruments.

wrong.0: Woodwinds use reeds or holes, but the trumpet uses buzzing lips.
wrong.1: Strings vibrate wires, but the trumpet is a metal horn.
wrong.2: Percussion instruments are struck, but the trumpet is blown into.

quiz.say: Which family includes the drum and the xylophone?
quiz.why: Both the drum and the xylophone create sound when they are struck or hit.

wrong.1: Strings need vibrating wires, which these instruments do not have.
wrong.2: Woodwinds require blowing air through a tube, not hitting it.
wrong.3: Brass instruments need buzzing lips, which is not used for drums.
